avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction reduces fluconazole levels and antifungal efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consider alternative herbal supplements

avoid_supplements.name: Rifampin (herbal)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 inducer significantly decreases fluconazole concentrations
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid use; select alternative antifungal if rifampin co-administration necessary

caution_supplements.name: Garlic supplements (high-dose)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential mild CYP3A4 modulation; garlic has independent antifungal properties
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for enhanced or reduced antifungal response; separate dosing by 2 hours if possible

caution_supplements.name: Grapefruit seed extract
caution_supplements.mechanism: Weak CYP3A4 inhibition may modestly increase fluconazole levels
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased side effects; generally safe but document intake

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: Mild CYP3A4 inhibition may increase fluconazole plasma concentrations
caution_foods.action: Avoid excessive consumption; occasional intake typically safe

caution_foods.name: Fatty meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase fluconazole absorption slightly; affects GI transit time
caution_foods.action: Take fluconazole consistently with or without food; maintain steady-state dosing

monitoring_notes: Fluconazole is a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor and substrate; monitor for QT prolongation (especially with concurrent QT-prolonging agents) and hepatic function in prolonged therapy. Most food/supplement interactions are low-severity; focus primarily on avoiding potent CYP inducers that compromise antifungal efficacy.
